real_s1.explanation: The unit responds to canids and similar animals (foxes, wolves, dogs, hyenas, lesser pandas, shorebirds). Within these classes it is most active when the subject faces or points to the right. It also prefers sharp, centered subjects in photos without a color tint, and it is weaker on left-facing subjects, cool-tinted photos, and subjects in the left third of the frame. Its rightward-facing preference is particular to it, since the similar units do not share it.

real_s2.explanation: The unit responds to dog-like canids and similar mammals (foxes, wolves, dingoes, hounds) and to some shorebirds. Within those classes it fires most when the main subject faces or points to the right, and least when it faces left. Its response is also stronger when the subject is centered, sharp, untinted, and seen against natural backgrounds with no strong straight lines. The rightward-facing preference is the most distinctive trait, since the similar units do not show it.

real_s3.explanation: The unit prefers canid- and fox-like animals (dogs, wolves, foxes, hyena, lesser panda) that face or point to the right. It responds most to right-facing subjects compared with left-facing ones. It also favors subjects that are centered, sharp, and untinted, against natural backgrounds with no straight lines. The right-facing preference is specific to this unit, since its similar units do not share it. The color-tint, horizon, and sharpness effects are weaker but also unusual for this layer.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds to canids and other tawny or reddish mammals such as foxes, wolves, dingos and hounds, plus a few shore birds. Within these classes, no photo property stands out strongly; none of the comparisons reaches the 95th percentile. The weak leads are that it is more active when the subject sits off-center to the right, when the photo has a cool blue or green tint (and, more weakly, a warm tint) rather than none, and when the subject is either very large or small in the frame rather than medium. One similar unit also scores high on the cool-tint comparison. These picks are tentative because the groups are small.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds to canids and other tawny-coated mammals: wild and domestic dogs, foxes, hyena, red panda, plus a few birds and a soccer ball. Within these classes no photo property stands out strongly; nothing reaches the 95th percentile. The weak tendencies are that it is more active when the subject sits in the right third of the frame and when the photo has a color tint, especially a cool blue or green tint. It is also somewhat more active when the subject either fills most of the frame or is small, rather than medium-sized. The cool-tint effect is partly shared with similar unit 3, while the right-third placement effect is not shared.

null_s3.explanation: No row reaches the 95th percentile, so this unit has no strong distinctive photo-property preference on these canid- and fox-heavy classes. It mostly responds to the class content itself (dogs, wolves, foxes, reddish-brown fur). The weak trends point to more activity when the photo has a color tint, especially a cool blue or green one, when the subject sits off to the right of the frame, and when the subject either fills most of the frame or is small rather than medium-sized. The tint and right-of-frame effects are the strongest, at the 93rd percentile, and their similar units mostly do not share them. Row 16 is less clear-cut, since one similar unit is at 96. All of these rest on few photos, so they are low-confidence picks.
